preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, int) for x in stdin.split() if x.isdigit()) and len(stdin.split()) == 2 + int(stdin.split()[0])
preconditions.description: The first line contains exactly two integers N and K (2 ≤ N ≤ 100000, 0 ≤ K ≤ min(10, N-2)), and the second line contains exactly N space-separated integers A₁, A₂, ..., Aₙ (−10⁹ ≤ Aᵢ ≤ 10⁹).

preconditions.expression: N >= 2 and K >= 0 and K <= min(10, N - 2)
preconditions.description: N is at least 2, and K is non-negative and does not exceed min(10, N-2).

postconditions.description: The output is a single line containing N space-separated integers representing the resulting arithmetic progression array.

postconditions.expression: all(result_array[i] == a0 + i * d for i in range(N)) for some a0, d in (lambda arr: [(arr[0], arr[1] - arr[0])] if len(arr) >= 2 else [(arr[0], 0)])(result_array)
postconditions.description: The output array is an arithmetic progression defined by a₀ and d, where aᵢ = a₀ + i * d for all i in 0..N-1.

postconditions.expression: sum(1 for i in range(N) if result_array[i] != original_array[i]) <= K
postconditions.description: The number of changes made to the original array to form the arithmetic progression is at most K.

postconditions.expression: not any((a0 < result_a0) or (a0 == result_a0 and d < result_d) for a0, d in candidate_pairs if candidate_pairs != [(result_a0, result_d)])
postconditions.description: Among all possible arithmetic progressions with at most K changes, the output is the most beautiful one, where beauty is defined as (a₀ < b₀) or (a₀ == b₀ and d₀ < d₁). Here, candidate_pairs is the set of all valid (a₀, d) pairs that satisfy Q2 and Q3.
